subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a militarized 6x6 truck design with an armored cab, missile turret on the cargo bed, and neon glow strips, deciding to keep the wheels as simple static props rather than jointed parts.

I'm working out dimensions for the truck's chassis, wheels, and cab, picking a gunmetal and olive-black color scheme with neon cyan and warning-orange accents, plus decal textures like hazard stripes and HUD screens.

Now I'm laying out the chassis frame rails along the truck's length.

Positioning the wheel axles and shaping each wheel as a tire with a glowing hub, rim, and neon ring, oriented sideways along the x-axis, then adding armored wheel arches above them and starting the cab's front section.

For the cab, I'm extruding a side profile outline in the z-y plane to form the sloped hood and windshield shape, defining the key points from the low hood edge up through the angled windshield to the roofline.

Still placing windshield geometry...

For the right side mirror I just flip the direction vector, since the texture is symmetric. Now I'm designing the front bumper armor as an angled plow extruded from a trapezoid outline, positioning it low on the front with tapering height, and planning to add teeth-like spikes plus a neon underglow accent.

Then I move to headlights, sketching thin glowing light bars plus round headlight shapes on the front face, followed by hood vents and vertical exhaust stacks positioned behind the cab. I'm also laying out the roof sensor array with a lathe-built radar dish, antennas, and a light bar, then sketching the cargo bed platform with its base deck dimensions and sloped armor side walls before starting on the rear.

Now I'm designing the rear as a tilted missile launcher pod with eight glowing-tipped tubes on a rotating turntable, alongside a glowing reactor core in a cage and side ammo crates with label panels, plus considering a roof-mounted RWS gun turret on the cab. I'm working out the exact placement and slant angles for the bed's side armor panels using extruded profiles.

I'm weighing whether the missile pod should angle forward-up or rearward-up — rearward-facing tilt seems safer since a forward tilt would push the pod's front edge into collision with the cab roof.

Settling on a rear-up orientation: pod centered behind the cab, rotated 35° so the back end points upward. I'm working out the rotation math to confirm the -z end lifts correctly, then considering using an orientation helper that aligns the pod's local z-axis directly with the aim direction rather than manually computing rotation angles for each part.

Writing cylinder helper and tube grid positions...

I'll duplicate the reactors symmetrically at x±0.7, z=0.75, then work out fuel tank placement along the chassis sides, fitting cylindrical tanks between the wheel positions so they clear the tires in the z-axis while sitting near the rails at x≈±1.15.

Now I'm positioning the wheels at x=±1.2 with 0.6 width, which pushes overall truck width to about 3.0 once accounting for tire overhang; I'm adding box-shaped fenders above each wheel with a skirt plate on the outside, and checking whether the cab's bottom edge clears the rear wheel position at z=2.7.

I catch the overlap: the cab's half-width of 1.2 extends down to y=1.1, which collides with the wheel top at y=1.3 in the same z-range as the cab body. So I'm raising the cab floor to y=1.45 to sit clear above the wheels, and adding a central lower chassis block (engine armor) between y=0.8 and 1.45 under the cab, plus side skirts at the wheel wells, with a front plow planned next.

Checking overall proportions — roof height around 2.9 plus antennas to 4m puts the truck near 4 meters, chunkier than a real 6x6's 3m, but that fits the cyberpunk aesthetic I'm going for. For the wheels, I'm planning a 12-sided tire cylinder with tread lugs arranged in a ring around the circumference for each of the six wheels.

Still designing wheel hubs...

I'm estimating the total part count will land around 350, which should be manageable, and now I'm planning out the texture set: hazard stripe patterns for bumpers and panels, a HUD-style windshield texture, and an emblem design.

I'm also mapping out more textures: plate numbers, a neon billboard sign using a placeholder brand name to avoid real logos, cyber camo paint patches, window glass, ammo crate labels, and warning decals -- while working out how glow effects interact with textured planes versus flat-colored parts.

For the body paint, I'm layering a mottled dark camo pattern with panel detailing and rivets, confirming this panel effect works fine on box-shaped parts, and keeping the flat color count low since the procedural paint patterns don't count against that limit.

Now I'm sketching the helper functions for building parts — a box helper and cylinder helper that wrap the geometry creation with position, direction, and rotation options, plus a mirroring helper to duplicate symmetric pieces across both sides. I'm also setting up an extrusion call for the cab shape using an outline profile with thickness and bevel parameters.

Working out the cab's windshield geometry next, calculating the slope and normal vectors so the windshield panel sits at the correct angle within the extruded profile.

Now I'm positioning the side window on the cab face, checking its z/y bounds against the roof slope line to make sure it stays clear of the sloped windshield edge.

I'm also placing the door emblem below the window, the rear cab wall plate, and roof-mounted gear like the armor plate, light bar, radar, antennas, RWS turret, and sirens, then moving on to hood surface details near the top segment.

Adding hood vent slats and front grille with glow bar...

Now I'm designing the headlights as glowing boxes with cyan-white light and amber DRL accents, plus magenta grille bars, and shaping the front plow as an extruded beveled outline attached near the bumper.

Still building chassis geometry...

I realize the deck at that height would clip the rear wheels, so I'm raising it to y 1.5, keeping a small gap above the wheel tops. For rear wheel coverage, I'll skip the fender box approach and instead place thin wheel-arch cover plates near each wheel.

Still positioning fender lips...

I'll skip the side steps since they conflict with the wheel, and instead add thin grab-handle rails plus mirror assemblies at the cab's front corners, with rods connecting to small glowing mirror boxes. For the bed, I'm setting up the deck dimensions and building side armor walls with an upper chamfered edge piece.

Instead of rotating the chamfer, I'll go with a simpler stepped second wall panel, then add a glowing cyan neon strip along the top rail and a row of vertical ribs along the side walls for detail, finishing with a decal plane positioned between the ribs for a text panel.

Now I'm placing the decal in a specific z-range and skipping ribs there to avoid overlap, then building the rear: a rear wall panel with a plate texture, red glowing corner lights, and a hazard-striped rear bumper positioned to clear the chassis.

Next I'm checking whether the launcher pod's geometry clears the rear wall — computing its orientation vector, endpoint positions, and corner coordinates to see if the pod's front-bottom edge intersects the wall region.

Then I'm laying out the cradle structure: trunnion posts flanking the pod at the deck level, a turntable positioned at the deck center, and a hydraulic piston connecting the pod's underside to a mounting point below.

For the reactors, I'm positioning them flanking the cab at the back, each built from a base cylinder, a glowing inner cylinder, a cap, and four connecting rods -- checking their placement against the pod and bed edges to make sure nothing overlaps awkwardly in x or z.

For cargo detail, I'm planning crates at the rear corners of the pod, sized and positioned to sit flush on the deck without clipping the pod's underside, textured on all faces so they read as proper boxes rather than flat panels.

Then I'm adding rear-facing details: a tall antenna mast with rings on the left side, and roof-mounted gear on the cab including a remote weapon turret with base cylinder, box housing, and forward-pointing barrel, plus a glowing red sensor eye and a lathe-generated radar dish on the opposite side of the roof.

Placing a light bar...

Now I'm positioning exhaust stacks behind the cab around z 1.5, x ±1.0, as cylinders rising from y 1.5 to 3.6 with a heat shroud and glowing orange tips, checking they fit between the cab back and bed front without clashing.

Next I'm laying out ERA-style armor tiles on the cab sides lower down—a 2x6 grid of small olive-toned boxes around x ±1.22, y 1.65-2.1, z 1.8-3.3—then checking that placement doesn't collide with the door emblem decal, so I'm shifting the tiles below the window line to avoid overlap.

Adjusting the emblem position to size .6 centered around y 1.85 so it sits just under the window without overlap. Then I'll handle the underbody details—tanks, battery boxes—before moving to the neon theme, planning magenta/cyan glow strips along the cab side bottom.

Now I'm adding more neon accents: a thin cyan strip along the plow top and cab roofline, skipping the drone pad idea. I'm also setting up the paint materials (camo body, dark trim, iron plates, accent color) and double-checking wheel placement so they sit flush on the floor at radius .65, with the plow bottom resting at .5 and consistent cylinder orientation for both wheel sides.

Working out tread lug geometry...

Now designing the car's cosmetic textures: an emblem with a magenta ring and wing motifs, a cyberpunk license plate with cyan text and barcode, and a hazard-striped side decal.

I'm also sketching a crate label with "AMMO" iconography and a tinted glass window texture, while thinking through how glow effects interact with textured versus flat-colored parts to avoid material conflicts on painted pieces. Now I'm working out the geometry for a missile nose cone.

Positioning cylinders and cones along the pod's directional axis...

Still working out antenna rods, lathe outlines, torus details, and mirrored box loops for the grille bars and door seams...

Now adding small door handles, glowing exhaust tips, underglow boxes, floodlights on bed corners, and red rear lights, and rough-counting total object budget across wheels, antennas, and launcher tubes before writing the actual build script.

I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and glowing parts, plus importing only the needed utilities like createBuilder, rng, patches, stripes, svg, metal, panelled, and glow, while deciding to use patches/stripes for camo and plow paint and metal for the hub finish.

I'll add a plane helper for decals and windows, orienting it to face the correct direction so text reads properly from outside, and apply a subtle glow for the HUD texture and side window.

Now I'm building the cab geometry with its paint, roof, and rear wall, plus a glowing headlight box, then looping through the wheel positions to place tires, lugs, hubs, and caps at each axle.

Adding glow rings and checking that wheel outer edges clear the cab's front bumper and axle spacing before composing everything together for export.

Adding the tank straps as thin ring cylinders, then moving to the antenna mast with a tapered rod, height rings, and a glowing tip sphere, skipping the drone dock for now before finalizing the code.
